title: Mourning the old Israel: Fauda after 7 October
gist: An editor's notebook led by a review of the new series of Israeli drama Fauda, whose cast and crew were directly caught up in 7 October and the Gaza war; the series centres on blood revenge and ends as an act of mourning for 'the old Israel'. Shorter notes cover a new Sense and Sensibility adaptation and Rostropovich-Britten recordings.

insights.claim: The new series of the Israeli drama Fauda is built around tha'r, Arabic for blood revenge, specifically revenge for 7 October.
insights.speaker: Alastair Benn
insights.so_what: Cultural signal of how 7 October reshaped Israeli self-image; Israeli TV remains a notable export.

insights.claim: The series portrays Hamas commanders as disciplined, puritanical ideologues untroubled by the costs of killing, akin to unrepentant IRA members.
insights.speaker: Alastair Benn
insights.so_what: Reflects an Israeli framing of the adversary as ideologically committed, implying no quick negotiated end.
insights.quote: These are disciplined men of ideology, untroubled by the costs of killing.

insights.claim: The series climax is framed as an act of mourning for 'the old Israel' in which the drive for revenge finally fades away.
insights.speaker: Alastair Benn
insights.so_what: Suggests a cultural mood shift in Israel from vengeance toward mourning.
insights.quote: a complex and beautifully constructed act of mourning for the old Israel in which revenge, and the will to carry it out, finally fades away
